articles.hook: ChatGPT just got a memory that actually works.
articles.headline: ChatGPT's new memory system keeps your preferences across every conversation
articles.body: OpenAI has introduced a new memory feature for ChatGPT that fundamentally changes how the AI interacts with users over time. Instead of starting fresh with each conversation, ChatGPT can now remember user preferences, writing styles, interests, and context from previous chats — keeping that information relevant and accessible across all future interactions. This is a significant upgrade from the previous model, which had zero persistent memory between sessions. The feature works automatically: users don't need to manually save preferences or rewrite context. ChatGPT learns what matters to you — whether that's your preferred tone, technical depth, specific projects you're working on, or personal details you've shared — and applies that knowledge going forward. The real-world impact is substantial: professionals won't need to re-explain their projects each session, creators won't need to restate their brand voice, and entrepreneurs won't need to re-contextualize their business model with every question. This addresses one of the biggest friction points in using ChatGPT as a long-term collaborator. OpenAI is rolling this out gradually across ChatGPT Plus and Team users, with broader availability expected soon. Users maintain full control: they can view what ChatGPT has learned, delete specific memories, or disable the feature entirely.
examples: Tell ChatGPT your company's tone and target audience once — it remembers and applies it to every email draft forever.
Share your coding preferences once — ChatGPT formats all future code suggestions in your exact style automatically.
Describe a long-term project once — ChatGPT maintains continuity and context across dozens of separate conversations without you re-explaining.

articles.headline: Meta's SilverTorch Makes Recommendation Systems 23x Faster While Cutting Costs
articles.body: Meta has released SilverTorch, a fundamentally new architecture for recommendation systems that treats the index itself as the model, unifying all retrieval components for user-generated content under a single design. The breakthrough delivers dramatic performance improvements: 23.7x higher throughput compared to state-of-the-art approaches and 20.9x better compute cost efficiency versus CPU-based solutions — while simultaneously improving accuracy metrics. This is significant because recommendation systems power feeds across platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and Threads, handling billions of content retrieval requests daily. Traditional approaches separate the index (stored data) from the model (retrieval logic), requiring multiple passes and systems to work together. SilverTorch collapses this into one unified architecture, eliminating redundancy and bottlenecks. The efficiency gains mean platforms can serve recommendations faster, with lower latency for end users, while spending dramatically less on infrastructure — a critical advantage as recommendation systems are among the most resource-intensive components at scale. For entrepreneurs building AI-powered content platforms or search applications, SilverTorch represents the kind of foundational infrastructure breakthrough that could become adopted industry-wide, similar to how attention mechanisms transformed NLP. Meta published a full research paper detailing the approach, suggesting they may open-source or offer this as a technical foundation that other companies could build on.
